newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Tirana back to normal after five days of madness.
newsitem.headline: Tirana back to normal after five days of madness.

text.p: The Albanian capital Tirana returned to normal on Monday as the population heeded a call from the government and went back to work after five days of chaos.
The new all-party government created last week to restore order after a rebellion in the south of the country, in its first official decree, on Sunday ordered all people to return to work.

Buses were running again, government departments were working normally and shops reopened for the first time since army barracks were looted of arms in the middle of the week and gun law ruled in the city. Schools and universities were preparing to reopen.

Bank employees showed up for work, but the shutters remained as bank managers, clearly nervous that thousands of looted weapons are still in private hands, awaited orders on whether they should reopen.
Jewellers remained closed, and their shop windows were empty.
A spokesman at the Transport Ministry said it was hoped the airport, closed since Thursday, would reopen on Tuesday.

At City Hall deputy mayor Buron Kaceli said a few key staff had been working throughout the crisis, particularly those involved with keeping utilities such as water and electricity operating normally.

He said line engineers had been busy throughout the unrest repairing power lines cut by bullets as civilians fired their newly acquired automatic weapons into the air in celebration. One engineer had been killed by a stray bullet. Kaceli said.
He said the food situation was not yet critical, although wholesale stores were depleted, since most families had stock-piled staples at the start of the troubles.

However there was concern about supplies of essentials such as oil and flour, and Kaceli said he planned to appeal to cities abroad linked to Tirana by twinning agreements and other friendship accords for food aid.
